findings.title: CATL gets China approval for battery deal in consolidation push - The Edge Malaysia
findings.reason: The article reports that China's solar industry has seen top companies 'lose billions of dollars after a rapid build-out of factories outpaced growth in demand.' It also highlights that Beijing has warned battery makers against 'destructive price wars that have damaged solar and other renewable-energy industries' and suspended construction of new power and energy-storage battery projects pending a capacity review.

articles.title: Japan's AI Beneficiaries: From OpenAI Exposure to Advanced Chip Packaging
articles.claim_summary: Japan offers a differentiated route into the AI supply chain via AI infrastructure exposure, advanced chip packaging, and machine vision beneficiaries.

findings.title: SB Energy to sell up to US$500 mil in shares to Japan investors as part of US IPO - The Edge Malaysia
findings.reason: The article reports that SoftBank Group-backed data center developer SB Energy is raising capital from Japanese investors to build AI data centers and power infrastructure, with OpenAI holding roughly US$5.5 billion in warrants and Nvidia investing US$1.5 billion. This directly illustrates Japan-linked AI infrastructure exposure and direct ties to OpenAI.

articles.title: Top Performing Fund for July 2026 - AHAM New China Tracker Fund
articles.claim_summary: AHAM New China Tracker Fund, benchmarked to the S&P New China Sectors Ex A-Shares Index (Chinese consumption and services-oriented "new economy" companies, not old-economy/state-owned firms), was the top performing fund for July 2026, reflecting strong performance in China's new-economy consumer and services sector.

findings.title: China's factories rev up but slower consumption highlights deepening economic imbalances - The Edge Malaysia
findings.reason: The article reports that China's retail sales rose only 0.4% in August (slowing from 0.6% in July and missing expectations), citing 'sluggish consumption' and 'weak household spending' that weigh on domestic demand, directly undercutting the claim of strong performance in China's consumer and services sectors.

findings.title: China's August retail sales miss forecast while investment slump deepens, piling pressure on Beijing - CNBC
findings.reason: The article highlights that China's retail sales grew by only 0.4% in August, missing forecasts and slowing from July, alongside an acute domestic imbalance between 'strong supply and weak demand', contradicting the claim of strong performance in China's new-economy consumer and services sector.
